message.content:
- Cut generic framing: “Important Notice” and “Please note” add no information; lead with the closure.
- Delete or ground unsupported details: “usual gathering area,” “committee member,” “garden tasks,” “essential repair,” and “thriving.” Only “Mina coordinates volunteers” is source-backed.
- Check date inference: “Sunday 19 April” is likely correct if 18 April is Saturday, but the brief only says “Sunday.” Confirm before stating.
- Reduce artificial transitions: “During this time,” “If you have questions,” and “Thank you to everyone…” feel like filler. Use direct logistics instead.
- Fix redundancies: “use the east entrance to enter and leave” can be just “use the east entrance.”
- Vary rhythm: four “Please” sentences create a monotonous polite cadence. Mix imperatives with short declaratives.
- Tighten volunteer section: “are still needed for the repair and garden tasks” is vague. Specify only the repair unless other tasks are confirmed.
- Tone issue: “essential repair” and “thriving” editorialize. Keep notice neutral and factual.
